question.problem:
The durations of direct flights on a certain route are normally distributed with a mean of $180$ minutes and a standard deviation of $20$ minutes. What is the probability that a randomly selected flight lasts more than $178$ minutes but less than $188$ minutes? **Round your answer to two decimal places**. *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4207\,$ $\,0.4168\,$ $\,0.4129\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5000\,$ $\,0.4960\,$ $\,0.4920\,$
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,0.2\,$ $\,0.5793\,$ $\,0.5832\,$ $\,0.5871\,$
$\,0.3\,$ $\,0.6179\,$ $\,0.6217\,$ $\,0.6255\,$
$\,0.4\,$ $\,0.6554\,$ $\,0.6591\,$ $\,0.6628\,$
The probability that a randomly selected flight lasts more than $178$ minutes but less than $188$ minutes is approximately {{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the flight duration (in minutes). Then we have $X∼N(180,{20}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(178<X<188).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(178<X<188) & =P(\frac{178-180}{20}<Z<\frac{188-180}{20}) \\  & =P(-0.1<Z<0.4)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.1<Z<0.4) & =P(Z<0.4)-P(Z\le -0.1) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.4)-P(Z\le -0.1) \\  & =Φ(0.4)-Φ(-0.1)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.4) & =0.6554 \\ Φ(-0.1) & =0.4602.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.1<Z<0.4) & =Φ(0.4)-Φ(-0.1) \\  & =0.6554-0.4602 \\  & =0.1952 \\  & ≈0.20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected flight lasts more than $178$ minutes but less than $188$ minutes is approximately $0.20.$
